title: OKR Dependency Resolver and Stakeholder Commit Contract
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable 'Dependency Resolver' process and an accompanying stakeholder commit contract that reduces cross-functional friction when company-level OKRs require multiple teams to deliver. The goal is to prevent untracked dependencies, reduce late scope shifts, and enable clear, actionable escalation paths tied to initiative milestones.
acceptance_criteria: Published Dependency Resolver doc with decision flow and escalation ladder in Confluence
Linear template for dependency capture created and linked to company OKR tickets
Stakeholder Commit Contract template reviewed and signed by 3 pilot teams (Eng, Infra, Design)
Automated weekly dependency health report surfaced in Console (OKR dashboard) showing status: Green/Amber/Red
Trial run with two cross-functional initiatives, showing at least one prevented unexpected blocker during rollout
tasks: Draft initial Dependency Resolver flow (owner: PM) — 2025-11-19
Workshop with Eng/Console/Infra to validate failure modes — 2025-11-26
Create Linear dependency template and priority tags (ENG/PM labels) — 2025-12-03
Build minimal automation that pulls Linear dependency tags into an OKR health report — 2025-12-17
Pilot with Initiative A (Console rollout) and Initiative B (Dedicated autoscale) — 2026-01-10
Collect feedback and iterate on Commit Contract wording — 2026-01-31
Scale to all company-level OKRs for Cycle 2026-W03 — 2026-02-28
comments: 2025-11-13 — Priya Nair: Kickoff meeting notes attached, major theme: too many implicit dependencies between infra and product features.
2025-11-20 — Oliver Chen: Raised concern about adding process overhead; proposed a lightweight 3-field template (owner, SLA, fallback).
2025-12-01 — Ethan Brooks: Automation spike complete; small script extracts 'dep:' tags from Linear and posts weekly summary to OKR dashboard.
2026-01-15 — Lina Gomez: Design feedback — stakeholder contract needs a 'carrier' section to declare UX risk and rollout phasing.
2026-02-10 — Marta Alvarez: Pilot 1 retrospective: dependency contract helped unblock a data schema mismatch; saved ~3 engineering days.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increased process can slow early-stage work — mitigated by a minimal template and 'trust-first' opt-out for small tasks
Relying on Linear tags assumes consistent usage — automation will include a weekly anomaly check to highlight untagged blockers
Contract signature may be perceived as legalistic — emphasize it as alignment artifact, not legal agreement
